examples.en: I trim the trees in the garden on weekends.
I had my hair done at the salon yesterday.
I cleaned the fish and put it in the fridge.

examples.ko: 아버지가 손질한 칼은 아주 잘 들어요.
examples.en: The knife my father took care of cuts very well.

examples.ko: 내일 손님이 오니까 집 앞 화단을 손질할 거예요.
examples.en: A guest is coming tomorrow, so I will tidy the flower bed in front of the house.
After shaping my eyebrows, I looked in the mirror.

explain: 머리, 나무, 생선, 옷처럼 다듬거나 정리해야 하는 것에 두루 써요. 요리에서는 생선이나 채소를 씻고 자르는 준비 단계를 '손질하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It works for anything you tidy or shape: hair, trees, fish, clothes. In cooking, it names the prep step of cleaning and cutting fish or vegetables.

examples.ko: 이 에세이는 여행 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This essay is full of travel stories.
I write a short essay every weekend.

examples.ko: 친구가 추천한 에세이 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I am reading an essay book my friend recommended.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 소설보다 에세이로 더 유명해요.
examples.en: That author is better known for essays than for novels.
You can feel the author's honest thoughts in the essay.
The newly released essay collection is popular at bookstores.

explain: 소설과 달리 지은이의 경험과 생각을 쓴 글을 가리켜요. 서점에서는 '소설', '시', '에세이'처럼 갈래 이름으로도 봐요. 같은 뜻의 한자어로 '수필'도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike a novel, it is writing based on the author's own experiences and thoughts. Bookstores use it as a genre label next to novels and poems. A Sino-Korean word with the same sense, 수필, also exists.

examples.ko: 영화사에서 새 영화의 배우를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The film company is looking for actors for its new movie.
After graduating from university, I got a job at a film company.

examples.ko: 그 영화사는 작은 영화를 많이 만들어요.
examples.en: That film company makes many small movies.
The film company will release the trailer next month.

examples.ko: 영화사 직원이 감독님과 회의를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: A film company employee is having a meeting with the director.

examples.ko: 큰 영화사와 계약한 감독이 새 영화를 준비해요.
examples.en: The director who signed with a big film company is preparing a new movie.

explain: '출판사', '방송사', '여행사'처럼 '-사'로 끝나는 회사 이름 중 하나예요. 영화를 직접 만드는 회사도, 극장에 영화를 공급하는 회사도 영화사라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is one of the company names ending in -사, like 출판사, 방송사, and 여행사. Both studios that make films and firms that supply films to theaters are called 영화사.

examples.ko: 이 색은 너무 옅어서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: This color is so light that the letters are hard to see.

examples.ko: 물을 너무 많이 넣어서 물감 색이 옅어요.
examples.en: I added too much water, so the paint color is pale.
I bought a pale sky-blue T-shirt.
You look natural because you wore light makeup.
The fog has become much thinner than in the morning.

examples.ko: 향이 옅을 때는 한 번 더 뿌려요.
examples.en: When the scent is faint, I spray it once more.

explain: 색, 냄새, 안개처럼 진한 정도를 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '짙다'예요. 묽은 커피나 차는 '연하다'를 더 자주 써요. 말할 때는 받침 소리가 달라져서 [엳따]로 읽어요.
explain_en: It describes how faint a color, smell, or fog is. Its opposite is 짙다. For weak coffee or tea, 연하다 is more common. It is pronounced [엳따].

examples.en: Every night I write about my day in my diary.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 쓰던 일기장도 아직 서랍에 있어요.
examples.en: The diary I used as a child is still in the drawer too.
My diary is almost full already.

examples.ko: 제 일기장은 귀여운 고양이 그림이 있어요.
examples.en: My diary has a cute cat picture on it.
I want to start this year with a new diary.

examples.ko: 일기장 속에 오래된 사진이 한 장 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old photo inside the diary.

explain: '일기'는 쓰는 글이고 '일기장'은 그 글을 적는 공책이에요. 그래서 '일기를 쓰다'와 '일기장에 쓰다'가 둘 다 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 일기 is the writing itself, and 일기장 is the notebook you write it in. That is why both 일기를 쓰다 and 일기장에 쓰다 sound natural.

examples.en: That singer's low notes are really cool.
Speaking slowly in a low voice sounds comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 스피커는 저음을 잘 살려 줘요.
examples.en: This speaker brings out the low sounds well.
My voice cracked on the low notes while I was singing.

examples.ko: 형의 저음은 깊고 부드러워서 라디오에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My brother's low voice is deep and soft, so it suits the radio.

examples.ko: 저음도 고음도 잘 내는 사람이 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy people who can sing both low and high notes well.

explain: '고음'과 짝이 되는 말로, 소리의 높낮이를 말할 때 써요. '저음이 좋다', '저음을 내다'처럼 말해요. 사람 목소리에는 '낮은 목소리'도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with 고음 and describes how low a sound is. Typical use is 저음이 좋다 or 저음을 내다. For human voices, 낮은 목소리 is also used.

examples.en: I pressed the bicycle pedals as hard as I could.

examples.ko: 페달이 고장 나서 자전거가 안 가요.
examples.en: The pedal is broken, so the bike will not go.

examples.ko: 피아노 페달은 소리를 오래 이어 줘요.
examples.en: The piano pedal makes the sound last longer.
The child stepped onto the pedal with a small foot.

examples.ko: 페달 없는 전동 자전거를 타 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried an electric bike with no pedals.
I adjusted both the pedals and the seat to fit the child.

explain: '페달을 밟다'처럼 '밟다'와 함께 써요. 자전거, 자동차의 '액셀 페달', '브레이크 페달', 피아노에서 발로 밟는 장치를 페달이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It goes with 밟다, as in 페달을 밟다. Foot-operated parts are called 페달, such as bike pedals, car 액셀 페달 and 브레이크 페달, and piano pedals.

examples.en: I got a new game console for my birthday.

examples.ko: 휴대용 게임기는 여행 갈 때 편해요.
examples.en: A handheld game console is convenient for trips.
The console suddenly turned off and I was startled.

examples.ko: 동생과 거실에서 게임기로 레이싱 게임을 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling and I played a racing game on the console in the living room.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 게임기 가격이 다른 곳보다 싸요.
examples.en: This store has lower console prices than other places.

examples.ko: 게임기에 연결한 텔레비전 화면이 아주 선명해요.
examples.en: The TV screen connected to the console is very sharp.

explain: 텔레비전에 연결하는 큰 기계도, 손에 들고 하는 작은 기계도 게임기라고 불러요. 휴대폰으로 하는 게임은 게임기가 아니라 '모바일 게임'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Both the big box that connects to a TV and the small device you hold are called 게임기. Games played on a phone are called 모바일 게임, not 게임기.

examples.en: I stared at a screen all night, so my eyes feel dry and scratchy.

examples.ko: 생선의 눈알을 보면 신선한지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell whether a fish is fresh by looking at its eyes.
The eyes of cartoon characters are very big.
I just rolled my eyes around, pretending not to know.

examples.ko: 인형 눈알 하나가 떨어져서 다시 붙였어요.
examples.en: One of the doll's eyes fell off, so I glued it back.
I made a snowman with no eyes and no nose.

explain: '눈'은 보는 기능이나 얼굴 부위 전체까지 가리키지만, '눈알'은 동그란 안구 부분만 가리켜요. 인형, 생선, 만화의 눈 모양을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 사람의 눈은 보통 '눈'이라고 하고, '눈알'은 거친 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: 눈 can mean the face part or the ability to see, but 눈알 points only to the round eyeball. It is natural for dolls, fish, and cartoon eyes. For a person's eyes, people normally say 눈; 눈알 can sound rough.

examples.en: One bundle of pencils is two thousand won.
I tied the newspapers into bundles and put them out.

examples.ko: 이 묶음은 열 개가 한 세트예요.
examples.en: This bundle is a set of ten.

examples.ko: 꽃 두 묶음을 사서 꽃병에 꽂았어요.
examples.en: I bought two bunches of flowers and put them in a vase.

examples.ko: 편지 한 묶음이 책상 위에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A bundle of letters is lying on the desk.
Bundled products are discounted separately at the supermarket.

explain: '한 묶음, 두 묶음'처럼 세는 말로도 써요. 대파나 시금치 같은 채소는 '한 단'처럼 다른 세는 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It also works as a counter: 한 묶음, 두 묶음. For vegetables like 대파 or 시금치, a different counter, 한 단, is also used.

examples.en: An error came up as soon as I opened the app.
I took a photo of the error message and sent it.
I keep getting errors when I log in.
The error went away when I restarted the app.
The screen froze because of an error during payment.
Even the same error looks different on each computer.

explain: 컴퓨터나 앱에 문제가 생겼을 때 '에러가 나다', '에러가 뜨다'라고 말해요. 같은 뜻의 한자어 '오류'도 있고, '오류가 뜨다'처럼 같은 동사와 어울려요.
explain_en: When a computer or app has a problem, you say 에러가 나다 or 에러가 뜨다. The Sino-Korean word 오류 means the same and takes the same verbs, as in 오류가 뜨다.

examples.ko: 화가인 삼촌은 집 근처에 작업실이 있어요.
examples.en: My uncle, a painter, has a studio near his house.
I painted in the studio until late at night.

examples.ko: 친구들과 함께 작업실을 빌려서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I am renting and sharing a studio with friends.
The studio is quiet, so I can concentrate well.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 새 작업실로 이사할 거예요.
examples.en: I will move to a new studio this weekend.
I bought coffee on the way to the studio.

explain: 그림, 음악, 공예처럼 무언가를 만드는 일을 하는 방에 써요. 회사에서 일하는 곳은 '사무실'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is used for a room where you make things, such as art, music, or crafts. A place where you work at a company is called 사무실 instead.

examples.en: If you follow the arrows, you will reach the exit.
The arrow drawn on the road points to the right.
I move through the menu with the arrow keys on the keyboard.
I marked the route on the map with a red arrow.
What does this arrow mean?
If you touch the arrow, the screen moves on.

explain: 방향을 알려 주는 '→' 모양을 가리켜요. '화살표를 따라가다', '화살표로 표시하다'처럼 말해요. '느낌표', '물음표'처럼 '-표'로 끝나는 부호 이름이기도 해요.
explain_en: It names the → shape that shows direction. You say 화살표를 따라가다 or 화살표로 표시하다. Like 느낌표 and 물음표, it ends in -표, the suffix for a sign or mark.

examples.en: I received a gold ring as a gift.
I painted the box a pretty gold color.
The river shines like gold in the evening sunlight.
Gold is flashy, so it suits a party.
My watch is gold, not silver.

examples.ko: 금색과 검은색이 섞인 옷이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like clothes that mix gold and black.

explain: '금색'은 색 이름이고 '금'은 물질 이름이에요. '은색'과 '은'도 같은 짝이에요. 금색 물건은 '금색 반지'처럼 앞에 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: 금색 is the color name and 금 is the metal itself. 은색 and 은 work the same way. Put 금색 before a noun to describe a gold-colored object, as in 금색 반지.

examples.ko: 새 매트리스를 사고 나서 잘 자요.
examples.en: I sleep well since I bought a new mattress.
The mattress was so hard that my back hurt.
This bed sells the mattress separately.
I spread a clean sheet on the mattress.
The hotel mattress was soft and nice.
Putting a cover on the mattress made it look neat.

explain: 침대에서 몸이 닿는 푹신한 부분을 말해요. 이불은 위에 덮고, 매트리스는 아래에 깔아요.
explain_en: It is the soft part of a bed that your body rests on. A blanket goes on top, while the mattress goes underneath.

examples.ko: 밤에 휘파람을 불면 안 된다는 미신이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a superstition that you should not whistle at night.
My grandmother does not believe much in superstitions.
That kind of superstition has no scientific basis.
It is inconvenient to be too tied to superstitions.
Even a story that sounds like a superstition is fun to hear.

examples.ko: 그 믿음은 미신일 뿐이라고 선생님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher said that belief is just a superstition.

explain: 과학적으로 맞지 않는데도 사람들이 믿는 풍습이나 생각에 써요. '미신을 믿다', '미신에 빠지다'처럼 말해요. 믿지 않는다는 느낌이 있어서, 자기가 믿는 것에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It refers to customs or ideas people believe even though they are not scientifically true. You say someone believes in it or falls into it. The word carries a note of disbelief, so people rarely use it for things they believe themselves.

examples.en: I like that the camera shutter sound is quiet.
The store shutter was halfway down.

examples.ko: 상점들은 밤 열 시에 셔터를 내려요.
examples.en: The shops pull their shutters down at ten at night.

examples.ko: 셔터는 한 번만 눌러도 사진이 찍혀요.
examples.en: Even one press of the shutter takes a photo.
The shutter was covered in graffiti, so I cleaned it.
I locked both the shutter and the door and left work.

explain: 카메라와 가게, 두 곳에서 모두 써요. 카메라는 '셔터를 누르다', 가게는 '셔터를 올리다', '셔터를 내리다'로 동사가 달라져요.
explain_en: It is used for both cameras and stores. With a camera you press it, while with a store you raise or lower it, so the verb changes.

examples.en: Adding green onion to the soup makes it taste clean and refreshing.
I bought a bunch of green onions at the market.
I slice green onions and store them in the freezer.
Green onions were expensive, so I bought only a little.
There are both onions and green onions in the fridge.

examples.ko: 대파로 만든 전을 아이들이 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: The kids eat the pancakes made with green onion well.

explain: 그냥 '파'보다 굵고 큰 파를 말해요. 국, 찌개, 볶음에 넣고 '송송 썰다', '어슷 썰다'와 같이 써요. 작은 파는 '쪽파'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a thicker, bigger kind of green onion. It goes into soups, stews, and stir-fries, and recipes say 송송 썰다 or 어슷 썰다. The small kind is called 쪽파.

examples.en: The heroine of this drama is a brave nurse.

examples.ko: 여주인공이 눈물을 흘리는 장면에서 저도 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried too in the scene where the heroine sheds tears.

examples.ko: 새 영화에서 유명한 배우가 여주인공을 맡았어요.
examples.en: A famous actress took the female lead in the new movie.
I was drawn to the heroine of the novel.

examples.ko: 여주인공과 남자 주인공이 처음 만나는 장면이 재미있어요.
examples.en: The scene where the heroine and hero first meet is fun.

examples.ko: 저는 여주인공 역할을 꼭 해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to try playing the female lead.

explain: 이야기에서 중심이 되는 여자 인물이에요. 남자는 '남자 주인공'이라고 하고, 성별 구분 없이는 그냥 '주인공'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the central female character in a story. The male counterpart is 남자 주인공, and the plain word 주인공 works with no gender.

examples.en: A singing contest is being held at school.
My friend won a prize at a photo contest.
I also want to enter this contest.
The contest starts next Saturday.
I was busy preparing for the cooking contest.
There are many singers who became famous through contests.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '대회'가 있어요. 운동 경기에는 '대회'가 자연스럽고, 콘테스트는 노래, 요리, 사진처럼 솜씨를 겨루는 분야에 어울려요.
explain_en: A similar word is 대회. For sports, 대회 sounds more natural, while 콘테스트 fits skill-based fields like singing, cooking, and photography.

examples.en: I went to the airport by limousine bus.
The bride and groom got out of a white limousine.

examples.ko: 호텔 앞에 검은 리무진이 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A black limousine was parked in front of the hotel.
The movie star came to the awards ceremony in a limousine.
This limousine is very long.

examples.ko: 공항으로 갈 때는 리무진으로 가면 짐 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: If you go to the airport by limousine bus, you do not have to worry about luggage.

explain: 한국에서는 긴 고급 승용차뿐 아니라 공항으로 가는 '공항 리무진' 버스도 리무진이라고 불러요. 어느 쪽인지는 앞뒤 말로 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea, it names not only the long luxury car but also the airport shuttle bus. The surrounding words tell you which one is meant.

examples.en: My mother finished girls' middle school and went on to high school.
There is one girls' middle school in my neighborhood.
There are many stationery shops in front of the girls' middle school.
My older sister was in the basketball club at girls' middle school.

examples.ko: 그 여중은 학생 수가 많지 않아요.
examples.en: That girls' middle school does not have many students.

examples.ko: 여중과 남중이 한 건물을 같이 써요.
examples.en: The girls' and boys' middle schools share one building.

explain: '여자 중학교'를 줄인 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '남중'이고, 고등학교는 '여고', '남고'예요. 남녀가 같이 다니는 학교는 '남녀공학'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of 여자 중학교. The boys' version is 남중, and high schools are 여고 and 남고. A school for both is called 남녀공학.

examples.en: I will get a perm at the salon tomorrow.
I got my hair permed yesterday.
My hair looks much fuller since I got a perm.
My mother gets her hair permed every two months.
Permed hair needs good care.

examples.ko: 파마하고 나니까 아침에 머리 손질이 쉬워졌어요.
examples.en: After getting a perm, styling my hair in the morning became easier.

explain: '머리를 파마하다'라고도 하고 '파마를 하다'라고도 해요. 파마한 머리를 '파마머리'라고 불러요.
explain_en: You can say 머리를 파마하다 or 파마를 하다. Permed hair is called 파마머리.

examples.ko: 커피에 시럽 한 번만 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please add just one pump of syrup to my coffee.

examples.ko: 팬케이크 위에 메이플 시럽을 듬뿍 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: I poured plenty of maple syrup on the pancakes.
Syrup is too sweet, so I add only a little.

examples.ko: 기침 시럽에는 단맛이 있어서 아이들이 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Cough syrup is sweet, so children take it well.

examples.ko: 시럽이 다 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The syrup ran out, so I need to buy more.
I made shaved ice with strawberry syrup.

explain: 카페에서는 '시럽 추가'처럼 단맛을 더하는 액체를 말해요. 약국에서 파는 달콤한 물약 중에도 '시럽'이라고 부르는 것이 있어요.
explain_en: At cafes it is the sweet liquid you add, as in 시럽 추가. Some sweet liquid medicines sold at pharmacies are also called 시럽.

examples.en: A gentle aroma spread through the room.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 아로마를 맡으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Smelling an aroma before bed calms my mind.

examples.ko: 아로마는 향이 강해서 조금만 써야 해요.
examples.en: Aromas are strong, so you should use only a little.
This shop also sells aroma candles.
I relaxed my body with aromatherapy at the massage shop.

examples.ko: 아로마도 좋지만 환기도 꼭 해 주세요.
examples.en: Aroma is nice, but please be sure to ventilate too.

explain: '아로마 오일', '아로마 양초'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 식물에서 얻은 향과 관련된 것을 말해요. 일상의 좋은 냄새는 '향기'라고 해요.
explain_en: It usually sits in front of another word, as in 아로마 오일 or 아로마 양초, for things related to plant-derived scent. An ordinary pleasant smell is called 향기.

examples.en: I picked a sofa after looking at the furniture catalog.
The new catalog arrived by mail.

examples.ko: 이 카탈로그에는 신제품이 다 나와 있어요.
examples.en: All the new products are in this catalog.
You can also download the catalog online.

examples.ko: 카탈로그 속 사진이 너무 예뻐서 샀어요.
examples.en: The photo in the catalog was so pretty that I bought it.

examples.ko: 카탈로그로 비교해 보니 가격 차이가 컸어요.
examples.en: Comparing them in catalogs, the price difference was big.

explain: 종이 책자뿐 아니라 파일로 된 것도 카탈로그라고 불러요. '카탈로그를 보다', '카탈로그를 받다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Not only paper booklets but also files are called this. You look at it or receive it.

examples.en: I listen to music with headphones on the subway.

examples.ko: 새 헤드폰을 사고 싶어서 가격을 비교하고 있어요.
examples.en: I want to buy new headphones, so I am comparing prices.
The headphones fit tightly on my ears and hurt.
I put my headphones in my bag so I do not lose them.

examples.ko: 이 헤드폰 정말 가볍고 소리도 선명해요.
examples.en: These headphones are really light and the sound is clear.
I made a call with the microphone on the headphones.

explain: '이어폰'은 귀에 꽂고 헤드폰은 머리에 걸쳐요. 헤드폰은 '끼다'와 '쓰다'를 모두 써요.
explain_en: 이어폰 goes into your ears, while 헤드폰 sits over your head. For wearing headphones, both 끼다 and 쓰다 are used.

examples.en: Before leaving, I stop at a gas station and fill up.
I filled up the tank on my way home from work.

examples.ko: 기름이 얼마 안 남아서 주유해야 해요.
examples.en: There is little fuel left, so I have to fill up.
You have to get out of the car while it is being filled.
I want to fill up on the highway, but the rest stop is far.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 주유해서 기름이 가득 차 있어요.
examples.en: I filled up this morning, so the tank is full.

explain: '주유소에서 주유하다'처럼 같은 말이 겹쳐도 자연스러워요. '기름을 넣다'라고 바꿔 말할 수 있어요. 전기차는 '주유하다'가 아니라 '충전하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Repeating the root, as in 주유소에서 주유하다, sounds fine. You can swap it with 기름을 넣다. Electric cars use 충전하다 instead of 주유하다.

examples.en: That singer's high notes are powerful and clear.

examples.ko: 고음을 낼 때 목이 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: Your throat can hurt when you hit high notes.
The high-note part of this song is hard.
The sound got thinner as it went higher.
I am worried my voice will crack on the high notes.

examples.ko: 저는 고음은 잘 못 내지만 저음은 자신 있어요.
examples.en: I cannot hit high notes well, but I am confident with low ones.

explain: '저음'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 노래방에서는 높은 음을 못 내는 사람이 '고음 불가'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with 저음. At karaoke, people who cannot reach high notes sometimes joke '고음 불가'.

examples.en: I put on lotion after washing my face.

examples.ko: 로션이 거의 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The lotion is almost gone, so I need to buy more.

examples.ko: 이 로션은 향이 은은하고 끈적이지 않아요.
examples.en: This lotion has a gentle scent and is not sticky.

examples.ko: 아기 피부는 로션으로 매일 관리해 줘요.
examples.en: I care for the baby's skin with lotion every day.
I received a bottle of lotion as a gift.
I packed both lotion and sunscreen in my bag.

explain: 얼굴 관리 제품은 '스킨', '로션', '크림'처럼 이름을 나눠 불러요. 모두 '바르다'를 써요.
explain_en: Face-care products are named separately, such as 스킨, 로션, and 크림. All of them take the verb 바르다.

examples.en: I majored in history at university.
We studied the Joseon period in history class.

examples.ko: 역사학과에는 책 읽기를 좋아하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: The history department has many students who like reading.
My older brother wants to become a historian.
Old records are very important in history studies.
History as a field is hard but interesting.

explain: '역사'는 지나간 일 자체도, 그 일을 연구하는 공부도 가리킬 수 있어요. '역사학'은 학문을 분명하게 말할 때 써요. '심리학', '경제학'처럼 학문 이름에는 '-학'이 많이 붙어요.
explain_en: 역사 can mean past events themselves or the study of them. 역사학 is for naming the academic discipline clearly. Subject names like 심리학 and 경제학 also end in -학.

examples.en: I got my room key at the hotel front desk.

examples.ko: 프런트에 가서 수건을 더 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I went to the front desk and asked for more towels.
The front desk staff were very kind.

examples.ko: 프런트가 오후 두 시부터 체크인을 받아요.
examples.en: The front desk accepts check-in from two in the afternoon.
The front desk is in the lobby on the first floor.

examples.ko: 프런트로 전화해서 택시를 불러 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I called the front desk and asked them to call a taxi.

explain: 주로 호텔이나 회사 입구에서 손님을 맞는 곳을 말해요. '프론트'라고 쓰는 경우도 있지만 표준 표기는 '프런트'예요.
explain_en: It mostly means the place at the entrance of a hotel or company where guests are received. The spelling 프론트 is also seen, but the standard spelling is 프런트.

examples.ko: 이 책은 실제 이야기가 아니라 픽션이에요.
examples.en: This book is fiction, not a true story.
I enjoy reading nonfiction more than fiction.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 픽션이지만 실제 사건에서 아이디어를 얻었어요.
examples.en: That movie is fiction, but it took its idea from a real event.
I picked a novel from the fiction corner of the bookstore.
Children grow their imagination by reading fiction.

examples.ko: 픽션에서는 작가가 이야기를 마음대로 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: In fiction, the author can make up the story freely.

explain: 반대말은 '논픽션'이에요. '소설'과 비슷하지만 영화, 드라마, 만화까지 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요.
explain_en: Its opposite is nonfiction. It is similar to the word for a novel, but it can also cover movies, dramas, and comics.

examples.en: I took out a sledgehammer to break a big rock.
This hammer is much heavier than I expected.
My hand hurt after hitting the wall with a hammer.
The nail struck by the hammer went in deep.
Both the hammer and the screwdriver are in the toolbox.

examples.ko: 육상 대회에서 해머 던지기 경기를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the hammer throw event at the athletics meet.

explain: '해머'는 크고 무거운 망치예요. 보통 망치는 '망치'라고 해요. 육상 종목 '해머던지기'에서도 '해머'를 써요.
explain_en: 해머 is a big, heavy hammer. An ordinary hammer is called 망치. In the track-and-field event 해머던지기, 해머 is also the word used.

en: arranged meeting for marriage; blind date with a potential spouse

examples.ko: 이모가 소개해 준 사람과 맞선을 봤어요.
examples.en: I went on a matchmaking meeting with someone my aunt introduced.
At the matchmaking meeting, we talked about our hobbies.
It is my first matchmaking meeting, so I am very nervous.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 맞선이 있어서 옷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I have a matchmaking meeting this evening, so I bought clothes.
The two who met through a matchmaking meeting got married.

examples.ko: 이번 주말 맞선에 입고 갈 옷을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose what to wear to this weekend's matchmaking meeting.

explain: '맞선을 보다'라고 말해요. 결혼을 생각하고 소개받은 사람을 만나는 자리라서, 가벼운 만남인 '소개팅'과는 분위기가 달라요.
explain_en: The usual phrase is 맞선을 보다 (literally 'see' a matchmaking meeting). Since it is a meeting with an introduced person with marriage in mind, its mood differs from a casual blind date.

examples.ko: 산에서 멧돼지를 만나면 조용히 피해야 해요.
examples.en: If you meet a wild boar in the mountains, you should quietly avoid it.
A wild boar dug up the field, so the farmer is upset.

examples.ko: 멧돼지는 코로 땅을 파서 먹이를 찾아요.
examples.en: A wild boar digs the ground with its nose to find food.
I saw a baby wild boar at the zoo.
I climbed a tree to escape from the wild boar.
There is a kid who is as strong as a wild boar.

explain: 집에서 기르는 '돼지'와 달리 산에 사는 야생 돼지예요. '멧토끼', '멧새'처럼 '멧-'이 붙은 산에 사는 동물 이름도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike the farm pig, this is a wild pig living in the mountains. Other mountain animals carry the same prefix, such as 멧토끼 (wild hare) and 멧새 (bunting).

examples.ko: 분홍 원피스를 입은 아이가 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The child in a pink dress is smiling.
The petals turned a light pink.
My favorite color is pink.
Pink and white go well together.
Pink gives a soft feeling.

examples.ko: 분홍도 노랑도 봄에 잘 어울리는 색이에요.
examples.en: Both pink and yellow are colors that suit spring.

explain: '분홍색'이라고도 하고 '핑크'라고도 해요. '분홍'만 써도 색 이름으로 통해요. '빨강', '노랑'처럼 '-색' 없이 말하는 색이 더 있어요.
explain_en: You can say 분홍색 or the English loanword 핑크. 분홍 alone works as a color name. Other colors like 빨강 and 노랑 also drop -색 in the same way.

examples.en: He is a religious person, so he goes to services every Sunday.
Religious people gathered and prayed for peace.
I read an essay written by a religious person.

examples.ko: 저는 종교인은 아니지만 절에 자주 가요.
examples.en: I am not religious, but I often go to temples.
Talking with a religious person gave me new ideas.
The pastor greeted everyone on behalf of the religious people in town.

explain: 특정 종교를 믿는 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. 믿는 종교별로는 '신자', '신도'라고 하고, 직업으로는 '목사', '스님'처럼 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to people who follow a religion. Followers of a specific faith are 신자 or 신도, and clergy have separate titles such as 목사 and 스님.

examples.en: I bought a fresh octopus at the market.
An octopus has eight arms.

examples.ko: 매운 낙지볶음을 먹고 물을 많이 마셨어요.
examples.en: I ate spicy stir-fried octopus and drank a lot of water.
The octopus is wriggling on the plate.
The octopus soup is refreshing.
Both octopus and squid are sea animals.

explain: '문어', '오징어'와 비슷하게 생겼지만 서로 다른 바다 동물이에요. 한국 요리에서는 낙지볶음과 연포탕이 잘 알려져 있어요.
explain_en: It looks similar to the larger 문어 and to 오징어, but each is a different sea animal. In Korean cooking, 낙지볶음 and 연포탕 are well known.

examples.en: My grandfather goes to the hospital because of heart disease.
Heart disease is easier to treat when found early.

examples.ko: 가족 중에 심장병이 있는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone in my family has heart disease.
Exercise helps if you want to prevent heart disease.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 심장병에 좋은 음식을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me about foods that are good for heart disease.
I visited a friend who was hospitalized for heart disease.

explain: '심장이 안 좋다'는 가볍게도 쓰는 말이지만 '심장병'은 병 이름이에요. '위장병', '피부병'처럼 몸의 부분 이름 뒤에 '병'을 붙여요.
explain_en: Saying '심장이 안 좋다' can be casual, but 심장병 is the name of an illness. Disease names are often formed by adding 병 after a body part, as in 위장병 and 피부병.

examples.en: I went to watch an ice hockey game in winter.

examples.ko: 아이스하키는 얼음 위에서 퍽을 쳐서 해요.
examples.en: In ice hockey, you hit a puck on the ice.
My younger sibling is learning ice hockey.
Ice hockey is fun, so I watch it every week.
Everyone cheered when a goal was scored in the ice hockey game.
I am trying both ice hockey and skating for the first time.

explain: '하키'만 말하면 땅 위에서 하는 필드하키를 뜻할 수 있어서, 얼음 위에서 하는 경기는 앞에 '아이스'를 붙여요.
explain_en: Saying 하키 alone can mean the field version played on grass, so the game on ice gets 아이스 in front.

en: older brother's wife (said by a man)

examples.en: My older brother's wife is always kind to me.

examples.ko: 설날에 형수가 맛있는 전을 부쳐 주었어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year, my brother's wife made delicious pancakes.
I gave baby clothes to my brother's wife.
My brother and his wife moved into a new house.
I call my brother's wife by a respectful title.
My brother's wife's hometown is Busan.

explain: 남자가 형의 아내를 부르는 말이에요. 부를 때는 보통 '형수님'이라고 해요. 누나의 남편은 '매형'으로 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is what a man calls his older brother's wife. When addressing her, you usually say 형수님. An older sister's husband is a separate term, 매형.

examples.en: The meeting hall is on the right side of the third floor.
Please turn off your phone in the meeting hall.
The hall was so crowded that we waited outside.
Guests are coming into the meeting hall.

examples.ko: 회의장 앞에서 안내 직원이 명단을 확인해요.
examples.en: A guide checks the list in front of the conference venue.

examples.ko: 큰 회의장을 빌리는 데 비용이 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to rent a large conference hall?

explain: '회의실'은 회사나 학교 안의 방이고, '회의장'은 큰 회의가 열리는 장소를 가리킬 때 어울려요.
explain_en: 회의실 is a room inside a company or school, while 회의장 suits the place where a large conference is held.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 알약을 하루에 세 번 먹어요.
examples.en: I take pills three times a day because of a cold.

examples.ko: 이 알약은 너무 커서 삼키기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This pill is so big that it is hard to swallow.
The pill fell on the floor and I could not find it.

examples.ko: 알약 한 알을 물과 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: I took one pill together with water.

examples.ko: 가루약이 쓰면 알약으로 바꿔 달라고 하세요.
examples.en: If powdered medicine tastes bitter to you, ask for pills instead.
Both pills and powdered medicine should be taken after meals.

explain: 가루로 된 약은 '가루약', 액체로 된 약은 '물약'이라고 해요. 알약은 '먹다'뿐 아니라 '삼키다'와도 자주 써요.
explain_en: Powdered medicine is 가루약 and liquid medicine is 물약. 알약 goes with 먹다 and also often with 삼키다 (to swallow).

examples.en: In autumn, cosmos flowers bloomed fully along the road.
I took photos in a field of cosmos.
Cosmos blooms pink or white flowers.
I picked a cosmos flower on a country road.
A butterfly landed on the cosmos.
I like delicate flowers like cosmos.

explain: 가을에 피는 꽃으로 잘 알려져 있어요. '코스모스가 피다', '코스모스가 흔들리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a flower well known for blooming in autumn. People say it blooms or sways.

examples.en: I drank coffee on the cafe terrace.
Our house has a small terrace.
I put several flowerpots on the terrace.
The weather was nice, so I stepped out onto the terrace.
The terrace is nice because of the cool breeze.
I want to move to a house with a terrace.

explain: '베란다'와 비슷해요. 카페나 식당의 바깥 자리도 테라스라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is similar to 베란다. The outdoor seating of a cafe or restaurant is also called 테라스.

examples.en: I turn left at the next signal.
The car in front suddenly turned left.
If you turn left at that intersection, you will see a bank.
Many cars are turning left, so the road is jammed.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어서 좌회전할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong road and could not turn left.
Turn left and go just two blocks, and you will arrive.

explain: 반대말은 '우회전하다'예요. 좌회전은 주로 차를 몰 때 써요. 걸어서 길을 알려 줄 때는 '왼쪽으로 가세요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Its opposite is 우회전하다. It is mainly for driving. When giving walking directions, 왼쪽으로 가세요 sounds more natural.
